rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Same-cwd recovery defaults to `--resume`, not `new`.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 174, the 'Connections blocker' trainer push (student walks in without the M4 artefact accessible — closed laptop, ran out of credit): '...Open a fresh Claude Code session in the repo and ask it to read what the M4 run touched.' At that point in the module the student is still in the base repo (the worktree fork per §7b hasn't happened yet — it's the NEXT section, line 48-54), so this is a same-cwd recovery and per §7c should default to `--resume`, not `new`. The harm is concrete and newly load-bearing: the brand-new '## Say what done-done means' section (lines 26-34) that immediately precedes this push-back is explicitly designed around the ORIGINAL M4 session staying alive — the maintainer note at line 124 states the whole trick is 'the transcript inspects itself before M5 reads it, with the original context still live,' and the prompt's own lead-in (line 30) says 'This one runs in the session you sent off. Its answer lands in the transcript you are about to read.' A student who follows the given push-back opens an unrelated fresh session instead of resuming the M4 one; the done-done Q&A then lands in the wrong transcript, and `diagnose-and-resend` (which reads the M4 send-off transcript) never sees the self-audit. The failure is silent — the prompt still 'answers' plausibly from repo state, nothing errors.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Reword the push to lead with `claude --resume <the M4 session>` for the same-cwd case, falling back to a fresh session (with the done-done section explicitly skipped, since a fresh session can't seed diagnose-and-resend's transcript-read) only when the session is genuinely unrecoverable.
